newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fyffes year pre-tax profit up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: Fyffes year pre-tax profit up 15 pct.

text.p: Fyffes Plc, one of Europe's largest distributors of fruit and vegetables, said on Monday that pre-tax profit rose by 15 percent to 48.5 million punts ($77.65 million) before goodwill in the year to October, 1996.

"The underlying strength of our business, our broad spread of fresh produce, the wide range of geographic markets in which we operate and the success of our recent acquisitions together have enabled us to produce a record result for 1996," chairman Neil McCann said. "We believe that 1997 will be another successful year for Fyffes."
McCann said Fyffes had obtained attractive returns from capital expenditure of 22 million Irish pounds and a number of sizable acquisitions made in 1996.
These included the purchase of 50 percent holdings in Italy's Peviani and Dutch-based Anaco International.
Last January, Fyffes acquired the banana business of Geest Plc for 147.5 million pounds ($241 million) with joint venture partner, The Windward Island Banana Development and Export Co.
Acquisitions accounted for 94 percent of a total 20 percent rise in sales to 1.43 billion, Fyffes said.
Overall operating profit rose by 23 percent to 47.1 million punts but Fyffes said profits from the group's continuing operations declined slightly.
"The overall increase derives from the operating profits generated from acquisitions and associated undertakings," the company said.
A geographic breakdown showed Ireland and Britain accounted for 28 million punts of operating profits, a rise of 15 percent, while profits in continental Europe were up 36 percent at 20 million.
Losses in the U.S. market were similar to the previous year at one million and Fyffes said its business in the U.S. has now been terminated.
The group remains on the lookout for companies to buy, particularly in continental Europe.
Fyffes said it finished the year with shareholders' funds of 200 million punts and net cash of 70 million, giving it the capacity to take advantage of attractive opportunities.
The company's share price was unchanged at 115 Irish pence by 0945 GMT. ($1=.6246 Punt) ($1=.6119 Pound)
